page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance features 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU includes a 25 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across several standard workloads, alongside some areas of lower performance. The instance achieves average ratings in static web serving throughput, Redis SET operations, and single-threaded gzip compression. However, raw CPU compute performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, falling into the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is average for both small and large blocks, but large-block write bandwidth is weak. Cryptographic and physics-based operations also score in the bottom 25%, and LLM inference with a medium 7B model is poor, though small 135M model inference remains average.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.cm4.2xlarge offers a stable resource profile for general-purpose workloads. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which, combined with the 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, makes it suitable for moderate web serving, text processing, and software compilation tasks. It is less suited for intensive database operations, heavy cryptography, or large-scale multi-threaded processing due to its weaker multi-core and write-bandwidth performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance utilizing a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor with 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating at 3.2 GHz, it features a 25 MB L3 cache and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show average capabilities in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and software compilation, though raw CPU compute metrics and multi-threaded decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is average, while large-block write bandwidth and database operations are weak. This instance is best suited for moderate general-purpose workloads, including web serving, text processing, and basic software compilation, where dedicated CPU resources are required but extreme multi-core throughput is not critical.
